report.scope: First sealed synthetic segmentation evaluation on previously unused supervision families; subsequent replays are regression only.

scope: Seal re-issued, not a new experiment. The layout-intent re-seal changed model/intent_v1/config.json, which model/boundary_v2/corpus.json pins in its provenance, so the receipt digest inside this seal went stale. The corpus rows are byte-identical (train/development/calibration/test all compared), the retrained candidate is byte-identical, and the held-out test was not observed again: only the receipt digest moved. The report was re-issued alongside the seal: its only differing field is seal_sha256, the digest of that seal. Every metric and the acceptance verdict are unchanged, so the held-out test was not re-observed.

config.evidence_scope: New synthetic segmentation supervision from frozen public reference lexicons. Partition by four physical leading keys before punctuation variants. New test families exclude the entire previously consumed public phrase-source vocabulary (including the boundary-v1 reserve and prefix corpus); the same lexical resources may know held-out words. This is not independent real-user intent or a new test of the unchanged context/prefix models. Fresh test opened only after sealing weights and a calibration-selected threshold. Old private/audit and published examples are regression cases, not held-out evidence.
